Conceptualization: set the main intellectual direction of the work
Data curation: reconcile and annotate records for reuse by others
turn disparate observations into a documented dataset
Formal analysis: apply a quantitative test to interpret the observations
derive estimates from the study results using statistical tools
Funding acquisition: bring in the award that paid for the work
obtain the budget backing from an outside sponsor
Investigation: carry out the procedures that produce the primary observations
perform the planned empirical work on site
Methodology: specify how the experiment should be conducted
devise the design of the study and its control conditions
Project administration: keep the work packages and delivery schedule coordinated
manage the project logistics and assign operational responsibilities
Resources: make the necessary laboratory instruments available
give the team access to materials and research facilities
Software: turn the proposed algorithm into a working implementation
construct and debug the computational tool used for the study
Supervision: oversee the investigators and mentor junior team members
provide scientific direction to those doing the day-to-day research
Validation: independently check that repeating the procedure yields the same results
verify the reported finding against a separate check
Visualization: design the graphics used to communicate the findings
create the visual displays and explanatory diagrams
Writing – original draft: prepare the first written account of the findings
Writing – review & editing: edit an existing draft and strengthen its arguments
critically revise the paper after the initial version was written
